sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: On-Site Factory Pre-Shipment Quality Control and Audit Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (International Company Legal Regime under the International Companies Act 1987)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: English common law statutory foundation supplemented by indigenous customary law (fa'a Samoa); unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax distinctions
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1999, in force 2000)
Samoa–New Zealand Double Taxation Agreement (signed 2004, in force 2005)
Samoa–Australia Double Taxation Agreement (signed 2007, in force 2008)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus, ratified 2018)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorism Financing Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorism Financing (Amendment) Act 2013 (governing CDD, enhanced due diligence and UBO identification); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2000 (establishing the Samoa FIU and reporting obligations); International Companies Act 1987, as amended (registers of members and directors maintained at the registered office in Samoa, confidential, not open to public inspection; nominee shareholding permitted with disclosure of the underlying beneficial owner to the registered agent; bearer shares immobilised with licensed custodians); Samoa International Finance Authority Act 2005 (SIFA as registrar and regulator); International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019; SIFA/FIU AML/CFT Guidelines (2018). Where no natural-person beneficial owner can be identified after reasonable exhaustive measures, the registered agent must record the senior managing official as fallback.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport for each director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the origin state is a Convention party; otherwise consular legalization through a Samoan diplomatic mission or recognized legalization agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution in the principal's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille when the underlying document is a certified extract of an official record; consular legalization for non-Hague origin states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or other competent authority of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization if the issuing registry is located in a non-Hague Convention state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or certified extract of the foreign register of directors and members (where a corporate or trust UBO holds 25% or more)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign registered agent or corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, with digital documents accepted where electronic verification by QR code is permitted under SIFA guidelines

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each shareholder and UBO issued by an AML-compliant financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution (signature verified by bank officer)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified banker's signature accepted without apostille; notarization required only where the bank does not issue branded letterhead with wet signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Curriculum vitae and professional business profile of the ultimate beneficial owner (for PEP detection and source-of-wealth assessment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Prepared and signed by the UBO or an authorized advisor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature page; apostille required only where the registered agent's enhanced due diligence protocol so prescribes

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement and perpetual screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories against (i) Samoa AML/CFT Act 2007 ss. 12–17 identity verification, CDD and enhanced due diligence rules; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists; (iv) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; and (v) Samoa FIU published advisories. ISIC 7120 commercial inspection/testing is classified as standard low risk; however, foreign and domestic PEPs, high-risk-country origin, or source-of-wealth anomalies require senior-management approval, documented source of funds and source of wealth, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. Any screening hit or anomaly triggers a suspicious transaction report (STR) to the Samoa FIU; business-relationship records must be retained for a minimum of five years after termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), International Companies Registry — name clearance is effected by filing a name-approval form through a SIFA-licensed registered agent; no direct public online portal is available, and pre-clearance is verified by the agent against the SIFA register of international companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Roman/Latin characters. Non-Latin scripts, including Chinese characters used by the traditional Chinese client base, require an approved romanized transliteration. A bilingual Chinese–English constitutional charter is permissible where the registered agent files a certified English translation; the Roman-script name governs. The name must end with the word 'Limited' or the abbreviation 'Ltd.' and must not be identical or deceptively similar to any name already registered or reserved under the International Companies Act 1987.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank; Banking; Finance; Financial (requires a banking licence)
Insurance; Assurance; Reinsurance (requires an insurance licence)
Trust; Trustee; Trust Company (requires a trust licence under the International Trusts Act 1987)
Mutual Fund; Fund; Investment (requires a fund manager licence)
Building Society; Chamber of Commerce; University; College (requires prior ministerial approval)
Government; National; Municipal; Royal; Crown; Samoan Government (suggests state patronage and is refused)
Terms in the Samoan language implying public authority or misleading professional qualifications
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar at SIFA within 14 days of the refusal notice, attaching evidence of legitimate interest such as a foreign trademark registration, existing charter, or prior trading name. If the Registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal by way of originating motion to the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days of the reconsideration decision. Reservation is automatically lapsed if incorporation is not completed within 30 days; re-filing with a fresh fee is required. No extension of an already-lapsed reservation is granted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Pure virtual offices are not permissible. Every International Company must continuously maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the premises of a SIFA-licensed registered agent, and must keep at that office the register of members, register of directors, and any corporate seal. Remote conduct of the ISIC 7120 factory-inspection business from abroad (e.g., China-based operations) is permissible, while the statutory seat and corporate records remain in Apia. No dedicated Samoan statutory licence is required for offshore ISIC 7120 activities; the mandatory endorsements are the SIFA incorporation certificate and the licensed registered agent. If the company later establishes a physical branch or employs staff in Samoa, a foreign investment certificate under the Foreign Investment Act 2000 and registration with the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour become mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate overall probability of compliance inspection in each financial year (approximately 20–30% portfolio-wide, with materially higher probability where the IC books related-party service income, holds a Samoan bank account, or triggers EU/OECD economic substance screening). SIFA conducts primarily announced examinations of registered agents, but unannounced physical inspections of the registered office may occur where an AML/CFT suspicion or enforcement trigger arises; IC records relating to ISIC 7120 inspection activities should therefore remain readily producible.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SIFA name clearance and reservation filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), International Companies Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: SIFA published schedule of statutory fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation registration fee for an International Company (standard share capital not exceeding USD 10,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: SIFA published schedule of registration fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office fee (first year, including name-approval handling, statutory filings, and record keeping)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for licensed registered agents (USD 700–1,000 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT customer due diligence and UBO profiling file (screening, risk rating, PEP and sanctions checks)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: AML/CFT Act 2007 compliance costs; prevailing market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of KYC documents (passport and proof of address) per beneficial owner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff or prevailing notarial benchmark of the origin jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certification (flat fee for two apostilles on certified passport and corporate documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority for apostilles in the country of origin (e.g., Secretary of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed fee per apostille certificate under the 1961 Hague Convention schedule

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Act No. 8 of 1987, Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018 and the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2021; see especially ss. 5-10 (incorporation by registration), s. 130 (registered office and registered agent), and ss. 97-102 (directors and officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, c/o Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (SIFA Form IC-1) accompanied by the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Company may adopt an authorized capital of USD 1,000 represented by no-par value shares and may allot shares without any escrow deposit or paid-up capital contribution before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscription to the initial ordinary shares of the Company be and is hereby ratified, and that [1,000] ordinary no-par value shares be allotted to the initial subscriber as reflected in the share register. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the Company be established at the office of the Registered Agent, Apia, Samoa, and that the Registered Agent be appointed to act for the Company in Samoa. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [Name of Director] be appointed as first director and [Name of Corporate Secretary] be appointed as secretary, each to serve until replaced by the members; and that the director be authorized to open bank accounts, execute service contracts, and arrange the industrial licenses required for the inspection and quality-control business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Corporate Registry via licensed Samoa registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name-reservation request through the licensed Samoan registered agent. The Registrar checks the proposed name against prohibited names, existing international companies and domestic companies. The name must end with the suffix 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or an approved abbreviation. Upon clearance, the name is reserved for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request letter
Consent of registered agent
KYC and due diligence pack on each proposed shareholder and beneficial owner
Proposed company name and suffix confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, file a revised request with up to three alternate names within 5 business days; no additional government fee is payable for the alternate-name resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association and Registered Agent Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent; notarized execution required for non-resident subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association in the approved international company form, the consent of the registered agent to maintain the registered office, and the consent of the first director. Each subscriber must sign in person or by power of attorney; signatures of non-resident subscribers must be notarized or apostilled. The objects clause must expressly cover 'testing, inspection, quality control and pre-shipment verification services'.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent of Registered Agent (Form IC-RA)
Consent of First Director(s)
Subscriber list and share subscription statement
Certified copy of passport and proof of address for each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects to the objects clause or name suffix, amend the constitutional documents by a supplementary memorandum executed by all subscribers and re-file without any additional government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia — official submission through the SIFA registry counter or approved e-filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit SIFA Form IC-1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, registered office consent, director consents and the KYC pack. Pay the USD 100 government filing fee by telegraphic transfer or card. Indicate whether standard processing (3-5 business days) or expedited processing (24 hours) is required.
required_dossiers: SIFA Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation)
Original or certified true copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consents of registered agent, director(s), and secretary
Beneficial ownership and KYC documentation
Evidence of payment of the USD 100 government filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Registrar may issue a requisition letter; a curative response must be filed through the registered agent within 14 days. If the deadline is missed, re-file with a new application and a statutory declaration explaining the delay; the already paid fee is credited to the re-filed application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registrar examines the application, registers the company, and issues a Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company registration number and the date of incorporation. The International Company exists as a body corporate with limited liability from the certificate date. Verify the certificate details and the registered office entry in the SIFA corporate registry extract.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
SIFA corporate registry extract for the newly formed company
Certificate of Registered Office (Form IC-ROC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a clerical error appears in the certificate (company name, registration number, or date), apply to the Registrar for administrative correction supported by a statutory declaration; the corrective certificate is issued within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance: Appointments, Share Certificates, and Bank Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors of the Company; SIFA oversees the associated beneficial ownership filing obligation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting by paper resolution. Pass the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution establishing the registered office, ratifying the share subscription and allotment, and appointing the first director and secretary. Issue share certificates to the initial subscriber, adopt a common seal if desired, and open a corporate bank or e-money account (wire transfer and Wise) for collection of inspection fees.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (as worded in this dossier)
Share certificates and register of members
Register of directors and secretary
Bank or e-money account application with the Certificate of Incorporation and certified board resolution
Registered agent certificate of good standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment service provider queries the corporate resolution, obtain a certified extract of the resolution from the Samoa registered agent and resubmit; if a director's identity document is rejected, supply an apostilled passport copy within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Register Filing and Annual Government Fee Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — Beneficial Ownership Compliance Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial copy of the beneficial ownership register with SIFA within 30 days of incorporation and update it within 14 days of any change. Pay the annual government license fee of USD 150 on or before each incorporation anniversary to keep the International Company in good standing.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership register (initial SIFA filing)
Annual government license fee remittance of USD 150
Registered agent confirmation for the current corporate year
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late payment triggers a reinstatement fee and penalty; apply for administrative reinstatement through the registered agent within 12 months if the company is struck off. If SIFA raises a query on the beneficial ownership register, submit a corrective filing with supporting certification from the registered agent within 14 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — Business Licencing Division; Samoa Bureau of Standards (SBS) for conformity assessment and laboratory accreditation
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence under the Business Licences Act 1998 (MCIL) and, where an on-island testing laboratory is operated, Technical Testing / Inspection Accreditation under the Samoa Bureau of Standards Act 2016 (ISO/IEC 17025)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Low-impact commercial activity: registration-level environmental clearance is required for an inspection agency office; a Category B preliminary environmental assessment (PEA) applies only if a physical testing laboratory with chemical reagents, effluent discharge, or hazardous waste streams is established on-island.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: zero discharge of trade effluent to stormwater; sanitary effluent must meet Samoa wastewater standards (pH 6-9, BOD ≤ 30 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L). VOCs: solvent-based reagents must be stored in certified cabinets and occupational air exposure must respect applicable threshold limit values with no uncontrolled fume release. Waste handling: hazardous laboratory waste must be segregated, labeled, and transported by a PUMA-licensed waste contractor under the Waste Management Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection Certificate issued by the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) for the registered office and laboratory premises; building structural-load and occupancy clearance (development consent) from PUMA under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; and an occupational health certificate of compliance from MCIL confirming safe workplace conditions for inspection personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa, operating under the Tax Administration Act 2012 and the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2007; official e-services portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the International Company (IC) with the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), under the International Companies Act 1987, and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and the Register of Directors and Secretary. Step 2: Submit the prescribed Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) application to the Commissioner of the Ministry for Revenue, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, the charter/memorandum and articles of association, registered office address in Samoa, names and addresses of all directors and shareholders, and certified passport copies. Step 3: The Ministry for Revenue verifies the documents and issues the TIN for the IC. Step 4 (separate registration): If the IC makes taxable supplies in Samoa connected with domestic business above the VAGST threshold, it must separately file a VAGST registration return with the Ministry for Revenue; a purely offshore IC undertaking only international inspection and quality-control services for non-resident principals is generally not required to register for VAGST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: An International Company incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 is statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax, dividend withholding tax, capital gains duty, stamp duty, and repatriation tax on all international business income and transactions for 20 years from the date of incorporation, as evidenced by a Tax Exemption Certificate obtainable from the Registrar. The exemption is confined to the IC's offshore business; any unauthorized domestic Samoan-source business would fall within the taxing net of the Income Tax Act 2012. Territorial scope is therefore limited to offshore operations, and the entity is not a tax resident subject to net-basis taxation for its exempt international activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not provide a US-style check-the-box regime and has no domestic hybrid mismatch election. Available elections and mechanisms are: (a) application to the Registrar for a Tax Exemption Certificate under the International Companies Act 1987, evidencing the IC's automatic 20-year tax-exempt status; (b) optional voluntary registration for VAGST under the VAGST Act 2007 where the compulsory threshold is not exceeded; (c) conversion between International Company, Foreign Company, and Local Company status by registrar application, which prospectively changes the entity's tax classification; and (d) the IC may elect to obtain a ruling from the Ministry for Revenue on the treatment of a specific international service transaction, although no elective entity-classification or hybrid rules exist.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST), governed by the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2007, as amended, administered by the Ministry for Revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (Samoan Tala) of taxable supplies in any 12-month period. Supplies of inspection, testing, and quality-control services by an IC to non-resident principals for use outside Samoa are zero-rated or out of scope and therefore do not count toward the registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping system is currently in force in Samoa. Taxpayers must retain and, on request, produce compliant tax invoices containing the supplier's name and TIN, sequential invoice number, invoice date, description of the supply, quantity, price, and the VAGST amount. Returns are filed electronically or in paper form through the Ministry for Revenue e-Services portal. Samoa's digital tax roadmap contemplates phased enhancement of electronic filing and data-matching, but no operational machine-readable clearance or fiscal stamping mandate applies to service exporters.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) goods physically exported from Samoa within the statutory timeframe and (ii) services supplied to a non-resident for use entirely outside Samoa, as provided under the VAGST Act 2007. For an on-site factory pre-shipment quality-control and inspection agency, the service must be rendered to an offshore principal, the principal must be a non-resident, the inspection/testing reports must not be used in Samoa, and the supply must not relate to land or goods sold in Samoa. The supplier must hold a signed contract with the overseas operator, detailed work orders, inspection and test certificates, and evidence of payment in foreign currency to justify the 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / electronic export entry lodged with the Samoa Customs and cleared for any goods or sample shipments leaving Samoa
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing physical removal of the goods or samples from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit confirmation evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in Samoa
Commercial invoice and the signed service contract with the offshore principal
Inspection/test reports, conformity certificates, and audit working papers identifying the foreign importer and the inspected supplier
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner of the Ministry for Revenue may audit export zero-rating claims and compel full production of export documentation, contracts, and remittance records. Where zero-rated treatment is applied without adequate substantiation, or where export documents are false or misleading, the Commissioner may retrospectively claw back the 15% VAGST plus statutory interest, and may impose civil penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall under the Tax Administration Act 2012. Fraudulent evasion or falsification of customs/export records may additionally result in criminal prosecution with fines and/or imprisonment, and the Central Bank of Samoa may impose exchange-control sanctions for failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tālā (WST) is not freely convertible outside Samoa. The current account is largely liberalized for trade and service payments, while the capital account remains controlled. Profit remittances by International Companies (ICs) are permitted under CBS exchange control policy provided the company holds a tax exemption certificate or tax clearance, submits audited financial statements, and the remittance is processed through an authorized dealer after a bona fide declaration. Dividend and branch remittances may require CBS approval for amounts above specified thresholds; unauthorized offshore transfers are not permitted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds from goods and services, including inspection and testing fees, must be repatriated to a Samoa-licensed commercial bank within 180 days from the date of invoice, bill of lading, or service completion, whichever is determinable. Unless an individual retention exemption is issued by CBS, 100% of the WST equivalent of export receipts must be surrendered to an authorized dealer for conversion into WST at the prevailing market rate. Retention in foreign currency is only permitted for designated offshore operating accounts with prior CBS approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific Samoa Limited (BSP Samoa)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low – Samoa does not recognize offshore digital EMI or virtual-account providers as authorized dealers under the Exchange Control Act. Any non-resident fintech/EMI account (e.g., Wise Business) can be used only for low-value ancillary operational disbursements and cannot lawfully receive export proceeds, capital injection, or settle Samoan trade invoices. All principal cross-border treasury transactions must route through CBS-licensed commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) for a corporate account opening of an International Company. The interview must take place in person at the bank's registered branch in Samoa; remote/video opening is not accepted for ICs with non-resident ownership. A prior remote document review may be completed, but account activation requires physical signing and original certified documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin corporate substance for a service-only inspection agency with no physical office or payroll in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement of Samoan registered office, detailed corporate structure chart, UBO passport copies, certified incorporation and good standing certificates, CVs and professional qualifications of the inspection technicians, at least two executed service contracts with international buyers, and a written business plan describing on-site factory inspection workflows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-frequency payments receivable from multiple overseas buyer jurisdictions with inconsistent invoice values
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level audit trail mapping each invoice to a unique inspection report and pre-shipment order; signed client engagement agreements; factory access confirmations; methodology templates aligned to ISIC 7120; historical bank statements for the parent or affiliate; corporate tax exemption certificate; and a detailed source-of-funds declaration for each counterparty above USD 10,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO nationality or residency located in a FATF-listed high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results from a CBS-accepted AML provider; negative media search report; sworn source-of-wealth statement; three years of personal bank references; economic substance evidence such as directorship minutes and decision-making records in Samoa; and a legal opinion from a licensed Samoan attorney confirming no shell or tax-evasion indicators.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from shareholders must be transmitted through SWIFT from a reputable overseas bank to the IC's operational account at a Samoan authorized dealer. The payment must be designated with the CBS balance-of-payments purpose code 'INV' (direct investment) or 'SE' (services), accompanied by a board resolution authorizing share issue, an updated shareholder register, certified incorporation documents, the inspection agency license, and an source-of-funds affidavit. Funds can be credited to a Capital Escrow Account before being reclassified as paid-in capital; due to zero minimum capital requirements, any amount in excess of declared capital should be treated as shareholder loan only after CBS clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for inspection fees and QC services must be made exclusively via bank clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for direct invoice settlements and Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) for contractual inspection and logistics bundles. Each outward transfer requires CBS Form X-1 or the bank's exchange control declaration, a tax compliance certificate from the Samoa Ministry of Revenue, the commercial invoice, and a copy of the final inspection certificate. Payment through informal transfer systems, digital wallet networks, or offshore EMI aggregation accounts is impermissible.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contract with a CBS-licensed authorized dealer for hedging WST/USD exposure on receivables up to 12 months
Cross-currency swap with a licensed commercial bank for multi-year inspection service contracts denominated in foreign currency
Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) limited to hedging non-WST net exposure, subject to CBS prior notification and underlying transaction evidence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: due on or before each anniversary of incorporation; 30-day administrative grace period allowed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 100 plus 10% of the annual fee for each month or part thereof; continued non-payment for 3 months triggers administrative strike-off; restoration requires payment of reinstatement fee of USD 300.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit via the Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: submitted together with the annual return within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate UBO confirmation attracts an administrative penalty of up to USD 5,000; persistent breach may lead to strike-off and referral for criminal prosecution under AML/CFT legislation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regulated Business Licence Renewal (if conducting on-site inspection/testing services from Samoa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Licensing Division, Government of Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year basis: renewal application by 31 December for the subsequent year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a penalty of 20% of the licence fee; operating without a valid licence is an offence and may result in a fine of WST 10,000 (approximately USD 3,700) and suspension of operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Standard Samoa International Company is exempt from statutory audit; an audit becomes mandatory only if the company holds a licence under the Samoa International Banking Act 2005 or the International Insurance Act 1988, or if its articles of incorporation require audited financial statements. No revenue or asset threshold applies to ordinary non-licensed international companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Samoa has aligned its domestic accounting standards with IFRS; an international company may prepare internal financial records under IFRS or another generally accepted standard but is not required to file statutory accounts with the Registrar).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) and the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Act, the registered agent must confirm the registered details of all members and beneficial owners at each anniversary date. When a share transfer occurs, the transfer instrument must be lodged at the registered office, the Register of Members updated, and an updated beneficial ownership declaration filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the transfer. The annual UBO confirmation is transmitted alongside the annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (resolutions of members and directors)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 750 per year depending on registered agent fees, nominee services, and registered office arrangements
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 5,000 for a certified independent audit if voluntarily required or triggered by a special licence

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% statutory corporate income tax rate under the Income Tax Act 2012; a licensed International Company (IC) is statutorily exempt on all offshore-source income, resulting in a 0% effective rate for non-Samoan commercial inspection, testing and QC audit fees.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IC offshore income tax exemption (0% effective rate); no Samoan capital gains tax; VAGST (15% goods and services tax) zero-rated on exported inspection and testing services; no branch profit remittance or dividend WHT imposed on exempt IC distributions to offshore shareholders; tax losses carried forward up to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual IC Declaration and Economic Substance Return (Form IC-ESD-1) filed with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) through the e-SIFA online portal; the Resident Agent concurrently lodges the statutory Annual Return to the Registrar of International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within six months after the IC's financial year-end (i.e., 30 June for a 31 December year-end); the annual government renewal fee must also be settled at the certificate anniversary to maintain good standing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, IC registration number, date of incorporation, registered office address in Apia, and resident agent name.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners are identified through the resident agent; the IC must state only its Samoan-registered particulars.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary ISIC activity: 7120 - on-site factory pre-shipment inspection, testing, and quality-control audit agency services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe services performed for non-resident clients exclusively outside Samoa; do not declare any Samoan-source activity without first consulting Samoan tax counsel.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of core income-generating activities, physical premises, qualified employees, and operating expenditure in Samoa if an ESR relevant activity is captured.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A factory inspection agency charging offshore principals may fall within the 'distribution and service centre' category; evidence of direction, management, and substance in Samoa must be retained; otherwise state the exemption basis with supporting facts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate value of inspection, pre-shipment QC, and supplier audit fees charged to related offshore entities, pricing method applied, and payment rails used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State that fees are arm's-length and settled by outward wire transfer or Wise from non-resident counterparties; no Samoan-source revenue is booked.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of director and resident agent, date, and declaration of truthfulness under the International Companies Act and Samoan AML/CFT legislation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An offshore director may sign; the resident agent must countersign where required by SIFA practice.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-payment of the annual government fee attracts a monthly late penalty of WST 100; after six months of default the Registrar may strike the IC off the register, and continued default leads to deregistration; false declarations attract fines of up to WST 20,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years under the International Companies Act 1987.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (CIT-01) prescribed by the Samoa Revenue Authority (successor to the Ministry of Revenue), lodged via the SRA e-Filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within six months after the end of the income year (i.e., by 30 June for a 31 December balance date); any residual final tax payment is due at the same time.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), company name, registered address, and income year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An exempt IC with no Samoan-source income is generally not required to lodge CIT-01; if filing is triggered by accidental Samoan-source fees, complete all fields and attach the SIFA exemption certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income derived from Samoa; offshore excluded income is identified and listed separately.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose nil Samoan-source income; attach a summary of offshore inspection fee contracts, invoices, and bank receipts proving non-Samoan derivation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses (travel, sub-contracted laboratory testing, technician wages, insurance) and prior-year tax losses carried forward up to 5 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in deriving Samoan-source taxable income are deductible; offshore expense allocations must be supported by contemporaneous records and arm's-length documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 27% corporate rate, tax offsets, and net tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an exempt IC, net tax payable is nil; the Commissioner may still issue an assessment to preserve the documentary record.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents during the year subject to final withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC distributions to offshore shareholders attract 0% dividend WHT by statute; a non-exempt payer must withhold 15% and remit with this return.
An offshore director may sign; the resident agent should not sign the CIT return on behalf of the company.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of up to 10% of tax payable; monthly late-payment interest at the prescribed rate (Reserve Bank of Samoa base rate plus 5%); a tax shortfall caused by intentional disregard attracts a penalty of up to 200% of the deficiency; officers face fines of up to WST 20,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years for wilful evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for qualifying International Company distributions (statutory exemption under the International Companies Act 1987); 15% final dividend WHT applies to dividends paid by an ordinary Samoan-taxable company to non-resident shareholders, reducible to 5% under certain DTAs for substantial corporate shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief where withholding applies, the recipient must: (1) confirm residence in the treaty partner jurisdiction and complete the prescribed relief schedule; (2) obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the foreign competent authority; (3) lodge the TRC and Form WHT-R (Application for Withholding Tax Exemption) with the Samoa Revenue Authority before payment, or alternatively claim a refund within three years; Samoa's DTAs with Australia and New Zealand generally reduce dividend, interest, and royalty WHT to 10% (5% for dividends paid to a 10%+ corporate shareholder under certain conditions).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident WHT: 15% on interest and 15% on royalties; under applicable DTAs, treaty rates of 10% for interest and 10% for royalties apply to residents of treaty partners upon TRC-backed relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa has no codified Local File/Master File monetary thresholds; the Commissioner may require transfer-pricing documentation where the IC derives Samoan-source income or where related-party arrangements distort the Australian or New Zealand tax base. For a tax-exempt offshore IC, prudent contemporaneous practice is to maintain arm's-length benchmarking and intercompany agreements whenever annual related-party inspection and QC fees reach WST 800,000 (approximately USD 300,000).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2022, issued under the International Companies Act 1987, impose an economic substance test on ICs carrying on 'relevant activities', expressly including a 'distribution and service centre' business. A commercial inspection, testing, and QC agency billing offshore clients must demonstrate in Samoa: (i) active conduct of core income-generating activities managed and directed from Samoa; (ii) adequate physical office, qualified staff, and operating expenditure proportionate to income; and (iii) timely filing of the annual ESR declaration with SIFA. Material mismatch between substance and revenue triggers penalties, suspension of the tax-exemption certificate, deregistration, and automatic exchange of information with foreign tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false IC exemption declaration or false ESR return; understating offshore inspection fee revenue; or concealing accidental Samoan-source income derived from performing quality-control services inside Samoa for a Samoan factory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2012, evading tax triggers a shortfall penalty of up to 200% of the evaded tax, a monetary penalty of up to WST 20,000, and imprisonment of up to 5 years; the Registrar of International Companies may additionally deregister the IC and revoke its licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and offshore beneficial owners who sign, cause, or procure false declarations are personally criminally liable; the corporate veil is pierced for civil restitution where the entity is a pure nominee; courts may impose travel bans, asset-freezing orders, confiscation, and director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a nominal IC with no Samoan office, staff, or management direction while collecting substantial pre-shipment inspection fees from foreign principals; failing to file the annual ESR declaration or materially misstating substance indicators.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2022 and SIFA enforcement directives, penalties include fines per offence, daily default penalties, suspension of the IC's zero-rate tax exemption effective retroactively, forced deregistration, and adverse exchange-of-information reports to OECD member states.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who permit the IC to operate without economic substance are jointly and severally liable for regulatory fines; personal disqualification from directorships, liability to restore diverted client inspection fees as equitable compensation, and criminal referral where offshore trust assets are treated as personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Deficiency and Suspicious Wire Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large wire-transfer or Wise payments for inspection work without maintaining client due diligence records; failing to record beneficial owners; routing fees through third-party accounts; or operating an unlicensed trust or nominee arrangement that masks the true service provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Samoan AML and Proceeds of Crime Act 2007 and SIFA directives, the IC faces deregistration, monetary penalties, confiscation of proceeds, and blacklisting from international payment corridors; convicted individuals are liable to imprisonment of up to 14 years for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and resident agents are independently prosecutable; they face custodial sentences, confiscation orders, personal travel bans, and permanent debarment from the Samoan international finance sector; courts will disregard the corporate form to enforce restitution against the directing mind.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Non-Compliance on Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest on shareholder debt, or royalties to foreign affiliates without operating the 15% statutory WHT; failing to apply for DTA relief before payment; or mischaracterising service fees as exempt distributions to avoid withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2012, the payer must withhold and remit; failure attracts a penalty equal to the unremitted tax, interest at the prescribed rate, criminal fines, and assessment of the IC as statutory agent of the overseas payee for collection of the foreign entity's tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately fail to withhold after notice from the Revenue Authority become personally liable for the uncollected tax as collection officers of the Crown; aggravated cases carry imprisonment of up to 5 years, confiscation of equivalent assets, and prohibition on leaving Samoa.
